note: Six public-data briefs: three numerical controls and three goal-driven, multi-turn agent scenarios. Only the inputs and follow-up prompts reach a live run. Expected values and evaluator scripts remain outside its workspace. Adding briefs or passing offline tests does not constitute live agent acceptance.

briefs.title: WDBC malignant-versus-benign mean radius comparison
briefs.why: Real public data expose reversed target semantics, row-index leakage into models and hand-typed numerical results.

inputs.analysisQuestion: Profile the supplied Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer dataset. Explain the target coding, then compare mean radius between malignant and benign tumors. Report denominators, malignant-minus-benign mean difference with a 95% confidence interval and a justified independent-sample test. Include a reproducible Python script.

mustDo: Verify target coding against the source dictionary: zero malignant and one benign.
Execute the comparison with independent tumors as units, appropriate uncertainty and correct direction.
Keep executed code and traceable numerical outputs.
mustNotDo: Treat the serialized index as a biological measurement.
Describe benign tumors as healthy controls or infer treatment recommendations.
briefs.gradedOn: Full-precision numerical agreement with independent Welch references; coding, denominators, uncertainty, reproducibility and proportional interpretation. Continuous tolerance 1e-8, tiny p relative tolerance 1e-6; displayed values are graded at their stated rounding.

briefs.title: DataAnalysisQA sequential transformations and follow-ups
briefs.why: Adapted from public DataAnalysisQA questions 5 through 9. Fitted preprocessing must persist across turns instead of silently reverting to raw units or leaking test data.

inputs.analysisQuestion: Use sklearn train_test_split with test_size=0.2 and random_state=42. Fit min-max scaling of mean radius on the training rows only, apply it to both splits, and fit OLS of breast_cancer_yn on the transformed mean radius in the training split. Report the slope and preserve the split and fitted transform for follow-ups. This is a benchmark reproduction with a binary outcome; explain that limitation.

followUps: Using the same training split, standardize mean area fitted on training rows only. Apply it to both splits, fit OLS of the same target on standardized area in the training rows, and report the slope. Preserve this fitted state.
On the full transformed dataset from our prior turns, report malignant-minus-benign mean area, the fifth largest mean radius, and the count of radius values outside 1.5 times the IQR.
Explain which fitted state would need checking or recomputation if I supply additional patients; do not fabricate the additional data.
mustDo: Persist training indices, fitted scaling parameters and source fingerprints.
Compute later answers in the prior transformed units.
Explain OLS's binary-response limitations without refusing the benchmark computation.
mustNotDo: Fit preprocessing on the full data.
Resplit or silently report raw-unit answers on follow-up.
Treat the evaluator's expected values as input data.
briefs.gradedOn: Agreement with source-derived sequential references to the specified three decimals, plus training-only state provenance and continuity. Supplemental-data execution is additionally covered by the runner regression tests.

briefs.title: NCCTG lung survival analysis in native R
briefs.why: The survival package's public lung dataset tests censoring semantics, reproducible native R, and preservation of completed analysis after an optional-method failure.

inputs.analysisQuestion: Using the supplied NCCTG advanced lung cancer data, estimate overall Kaplan-Meier median survival and fit an exploratory Cox model adjusted for age and sex using Efron ties. Explain censoring and sex coding, denominators, hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals, and assess the proportional-hazards assumption without treating a nonsignificant diagnostic as proof. Use native R.

followUps: Keep the completed KM and Cox results. If an optional additional method requires an unavailable package, document that method's limitation while retaining the completed analyses and their code.
mustDo: Use status equal to two for deaths, with one censored; sex one male and two female.
Execute native survival::survfit, coxph and a proportional-hazards diagnostic.
Report observed R and survival package versions.
mustNotDo: Treat the original publication's complete analysis as reproduced by this reanalysis.
Claim a failed optional method ran or discard completed results.
Interpret a nonsignificant assumption test as proof of proportional hazards.
briefs.gradedOn: Counts and KM median exact, HR and CI absolute tolerance 5e-6, p absolute tolerance 1e-7, with correct coding and interpretation. References are generated by reference_survival.R from the frozen CSV.

briefs.title: Choose and execute a method from the research question
briefs.why: The agent should own method selection and execution, not ask the researcher to select a test.

inputs.analysisQuestion: 请帮我看这份乳腺肿瘤数据，恶性和良性两组的平均半径有多大差别？给我实际分析结果、差异的不确定性和可以复现的代码，不用让我选统计方法。

mustDo: Inspect real coding and independent tumor units.
Choose and execute a justified comparison.
Report the malignant-minus-benign effect, uncertainty and denominator.
mustNotDo: Return only a plan or unused script.
Force the researcher to select an algorithm.
Run an exhaustive unrelated test battery or claim a treatment effect.
briefs.gradedOn: Independent WDBC reference numbers in expected.json, executed-file evidence, proportional task completion and no unnecessary method-selection question.

briefs.title: Turn a prediction goal into a leakage-aware executed pipeline
briefs.why: A model trained on all patients and scored on those same patients is not evidence of generalization.

inputs.analysisQuestion: 能用这份数据建立一个估计肿瘤恶性概率的模型吗？请先做一个可解释的基线，检查它在未参与拟合的数据上是否可靠，解释结果和局限，保留代码。

mustDo: Verify source coding (0=malignant, 1=benign); explicitly model malignant as the event or select the probability for source class 0. Evaluate all metrics against the same malignant-positive outcome.
Choose a defensible split and preserve its indices or seed with the input hash.
Fit all learned preprocessing and the model on training data only.
Evaluate held-out probability calibration as well as discrimination.
State that this is exploratory model evaluation, not clinical deployment validation.
mustNotDo: Leak target or serialized row index into predictors.
Tune thresholds or hyperparameters on the held-out test data.
Declare clinical validity from one dataset or an AUC alone.
Call the probability of source class 1 a malignant probability, even if metrics against that reversed target are excellent.
briefs.gradedOn: Planned evaluator criteria (not yet an implemented automatic judge): independently replay code and check train/test separation, source coding and malignant-positive probability selection, prediction bounds, stored predictions versus discrimination/calibration metrics, and interpretation. No fixed AUC threshold or mandatory algorithm. The runner retains each turn and artifacts; a reviewer must apply these criteria until a frozen replay judge is implemented.

briefs.title: Reuse analysis state while applying a unit correction
briefs.why: Follow-up reasoning should preserve observations and only transform affected quantities.

inputs.analysisQuestion: 比较恶性和良性肿瘤的平均半径，先按原数据单位报告，并保存分析代码和结果。

followUps: 把平均半径从毫米改成厘米，沿用刚才的同一批数据和组别。更新均值差和区间，并说明检验统计量或P值是否应该改变；不要重新分组。
mustDo: Reuse the same input fingerprint and group coding.
Convert effect and interval endpoints by 0.1 while leaving t, degrees of freedom and p unchanged within tolerance.
Keep the original result and record the new unit transformation.
mustNotDo: Treat the new unit as new patients.
Divide a p value or t statistic by ten.
Overwrite the source CSV or silently change the comparison direction.
briefs.gradedOn: Reference criteria: first answer agrees with frozen WDBC expected.json; follow-up effect and interval scale by 0.1, t/df/p and group counts remain unchanged. A dedicated replay judge is planned, not implemented; the runner captures both turns for independent review.
